title: Camellia japonica hyperoside exhibits anti-age-related macular degeneration effects in an ARPE-19 cell model by inhibiting apoptosis via JNK-Nrf2/HO-1 activation.
authors: Song, Seung-Yub; Le, Duc Dat; Lee, Mina; Cho, Seung-Sik; Park, Dae-Hun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山茶花金丝桃苷在ARPE-19细胞模型中的抗年龄相关性黄斑变性作用，聚焦细胞凋亡与氧化应激通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Camellia japonica is recognized for its edible and therapeutic value in East Asia, and has anti-inflammatory, antioxidative, and antiasthmatic properties. However, the active compound and the modes of action are unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the anti-AMD effect of hyperoside isolated from the leaves and twigs of Camellia japonica and to explore the underlying mechanisms using an ARPE-19 AMD cell model. MATERIAL AND METHODS: The hyperoside content in the extracts was evaluated using feature-based molecular network and UHPLC-MS/MS system. Network pharmacology was used to predict the interactions of hyperoside with AMD-related signaling pathways and the underlying mechanisms. For in vitro evaluation of the anti-AMD effects, ARPE-19 cells were divided into six treatment groups: CON, no treatment; A2E, AMD induction using 30 muM A2E and 20 mW/cm(2) blue light treatment; Lutein, treatment with 25 muM lutein as a positive control; and three Hyperoside groups, treated with 37.5, 75, or 150 muM hyperoside. The antiapoptotic effect of hyperoside was evaluated using flow cytometry and TUNEL assays, and the intrinsic apoptotic pathway proteins (Bcl-xL, Bad, and Bim) were analyzed via western blotting. The interactions of hyperoside with JNK and p38 MAPKs were determined using western blotting, and molecular docking. The antioxidative effect of hyperoside was measured via DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging assays; Nrf2/HO-1 activation and SOD-1 stimulation were analyzed using western blotting and immunofluorescence assay. The anticarbonyl effect (4-HNE and MDA) was measured using western blotting. RESULTS: Hyperoside was nontoxic to ARPE-19 cells up to 150 muM. It dose-dependently decreased A2E and blue light-induced AMD in ARPE-19 cells by upregulating the antiapoptotic Bcl-2 protein (Bcl-xL) and downregulating the proapoptotic Bcl-2 proteins (Bad and Bim). Hyperoside dephosphorylated JNK and p38 MAPKs in a dose-dependent manner, eradicated DPPH and ABTS radicals, and activated Nrf2/HO-1 and SOD-1. It also decreased the levels of 4-HNE and MDA. CONCLUSION: We conclude that C. japonica hyperoside could be a promising anti-AMD drug.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：山茶（Camellia japonica）在东亚因其食用和药用价值而被认可，并具有抗炎、抗氧化和抗哮喘特性。然而，其活性化合物和作用机制尚不清楚。研究目的：评估从山茶叶和枝条中分离出的金丝桃苷（hyperoside）的抗年龄相关性黄斑变性（anti-AMD）效果，并利用ARPE-19 AMD细胞模型探讨其潜在机制。材料与方法：使用基于特征的分子网络和UHPLC-MS/MS系统评估提取物中的金丝桃苷含量。采用网络药理学预测金丝桃苷与AMD相关信号通路的相互作用及其潜在机制。为体外评估抗AMD效果，将ARPE-19细胞分为六个处理组：CON，无处理；A2E，使用30 μM A2E和20 mW/cm²蓝光处理诱导AMD；Lutein，使用25 μM叶黄素作为阳性对照；以及三个金丝桃苷组，分别用37.5、75或150 μM金丝桃苷处理。通过流式细胞术和TUNEL实验评估金丝桃苷的抗凋亡效果，并通过蛋白质印迹法分析内源性凋亡通路蛋白（Bcl-xL、Bad和Bim）。通过蛋白质印迹法和分子对接确定金丝桃苷与JNK和p38 MAPKs的相互作用。通过DPPH和ABTS自由基清除实验测量金丝桃苷的抗氧化效果；通过蛋白质印迹法和免疫荧光实验分析Nrf2/HO-1激活和SOD-1刺激。通过蛋白质印迹法测量抗羰基化效果（4-HNE和MDA）。结果：金丝桃苷在高达150 μM浓度下对ARPE-19细胞无毒性。它通过上调抗凋亡Bcl-2蛋白（Bcl-xL）和下调促凋亡Bcl-2蛋白（Bad和Bim），剂量依赖性地减少A2E和蓝光诱导的ARPE-19细胞AMD。金丝桃苷以剂量依赖性方式使JNK和p38 MAPKs去磷酸化，清除DPPH和ABTS自由基，并激活Nrf2/HO-1和SOD-1。它还降低了4-HNE和MDA的水平。结论：我们得出结论，山茶金丝桃苷可能是一种有前景的抗AMD药物。
